result_text:
I replaced the two mock-folder rules in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393) with one rule: `.*[/\\](__)?mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`.

A folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as test code, whatever follows in the name. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`. The rule works at any depth and with `/` or `\` separators.

The match stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` are not test code. Files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` also stay out. Folders the old rule matched (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`) still match.

The tests matching `ScopingConventions*` in `codeanalyzer` ran clean. I didn't add test cases for the new patterns or run the rule against sample paths.
